description: Simulates an object dropped from a height and left to bounce, and turns its fall into gates and voltages

params.text: The height the object is dropped from, 1cm to 3 metres
The acceleration pulling the object down, from 1.622 for the Moon to 11.15 for Neptune, with Earth at 9.798
How much speed the object keeps at each bounce, 0 stopping it dead and 1 returning it to the height it fell from
Drops the object again from the height set by ALTITUDE, which starts the fall over

inputs.text: A trigger here drops the object again from the height set by ALTITUDE
Volts here are added to the drop height, one volt counting as a metre
Volts here are added to the gravity, one volt counting as a metre per second squared
Volts here are added to the coefficient of restitution, one volt counting as a full 1

outputs.text: 10V while the object is falling and 0V while it rises, so it gates once per bounce and the gates come faster as the bounces shorten
The height of the object as it falls and bounces, 10V at the height it was dropped from and 0V on the ground
The height of the last bounce, held until the next one, so it steps down through the bounces

notes: the display shows the object moving up and down the panel at the height it has reached
nothing is falling when the patch is loaded, so all three outputs rest at 0V until a drop is started, and they return to 0V once the bouncing has died away
